assumptions: A material subset of overdue invoices is undisputed, supported by complete performance evidence, and collectible.
Polish counsel confirms the mandate, communications, contingency fees, and external escalation model are lawful.
SME creditors will grant portfolio-specific servicing authority and accept relationship-sensitive reminder rules.
Accountant-originated cohorts can be acquired and serviced profitably after dispute and collection timing are included.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Polish legal opinions, signed creditor mandates, accountant referral commitments, cohort data on recovery uplift and time-to-cash, dispute and withdrawal rates, debtor retention impact, and contribution after partner, compliance, and human-review costs.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Combining a defined exclusive portfolio mandate, date-versioned statutory calculations, evidence completeness, and success-based pricing creates a clear control mechanism around a chronic SME problem, even though collections themselves are established.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Overdue invoices impose direct cash-flow loss and contingency fees avoid an upfront budget request; however, collectible volume and willingness to enforce statutory amounts against valued customers are not yet evidenced.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Low startup capital, payment only from cleared recovery, and automation of routine cases can support attractive economics, but long collection tails, disputes, partner fees, and low-value claims may create poor cash conversion and labor-heavy cohorts.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish SMEs with recurring, documented, undisputed B2B invoices are a broad market that can be narrowed by sector, accountant channel, and evidence quality; the actual serviceable collectible pool remains unquantified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Collection agencies, law firms, accounting software, and invoice-finance providers already address the workflow, and transparent calculations plus automation are imitable without exclusive channel or data access.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven servicing system can expand across sectors, accountant portfolios, additional creditors, preventive receivables workflows, and other jurisdictions, subject to country-specific legal structures.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Twelve-month exclusive mandates, resolution data, evidence templates, and accountant relationships can accumulate switching costs, but mandates renew, claims stay creditor-owned, and competitors can offer similar contingency terms.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The founder's finance and analytics fit, low capital need, measurable outcomes, and partner-routed legal work are well aligned, though there is no current creditor mandate, accountant channel, or demonstrated collection edge.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Late-payment rights and periodically updated official rates create a persistent calculable opportunity, but the packet shows no singular new market inflection beyond ongoing digitization and statutory enforcement.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accountants and bookkeepers can aggregate trusted access to many invoice-heavy SMEs and provide evidence-ready referrals; no partner commitment or acquisition economics has yet been tested.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A narrow undisputed-invoice pilot is feasible with modest capital and licensed escalation, but authorization, legal boundaries, complaints, debtor relationships, evidence disputes, security, and delayed cash require disciplined case selection.

highest_value_structural_change: Limit the initial mandate to creditor-approved, undisputed invoices with complete evidence and configurable relationship tiers, while pricing only on incremental recovery above the client's existing baseline.
main_structural_strength: An exclusive, portfolio-specific mandate creates a lawful recurring workflow position, while contingency pricing links payment to recovered cash and removes the buyer's upfront budget hurdle.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed advantage is not yet proven against mature collection alternatives, and neither collectible case economics nor willingness to grant exclusive mandates has been validated.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Creditors may deliberately decline statutory interest or standardized escalation to protect important commercial relationships, sharply reducing both addressable cases and recoverable fee value.
